global.text: Stacked {gold} in the coffers and {troop_count} men under arms. Now I just need someone to tell me what to spend it on.
Our banners flew over {fief} again today. My old sergeant would have called that a fine morning, and so do I.
Pardon the grin, but {troop_count} soldiers marching in step is a sight I never tire of.
Back in the first war we counted our wins on one hand. Now I need the other hand just for the coin purse.
Honest truth: {gold} sounds grand until the garrison comes asking for its wages. Enjoy it while the ledger is kind.
Good to see the young crews pulling their weight. Keep the cheering down, though. The ones who lost are still reading.
I will admit {troop_count} men is impressive. I will not admit I counted them twice to be sure.
Took {fief} with a smaller force than I expected. Patience and a dry powder keg did most of the talking.
Wealth buys a lot of swords, but it cannot buy a good night's sleep. Ask me how I know.
Congratulations on the spoils, truly. Just remember the fens still swallow careless folk, rich or not.
The marsh fog to the east is thicker than usual. Bring a lantern, and don't trust the ferry schedule either.
Anyone else's lag spike kick in right when the siege horns sounded? Server has been stuttering since dawn.
Rain again. Honestly, I miss the days when storms only came on festival nights.
Someone mentioned a shortcut through the hills near {village}. Check the old maps before you risk it.
Those new cartographers keep redrawing the coast. The mountains haven't moved since the first war, I can promise you that.
Ormerath's weather is like a bad tenant. It shows up uninvited and leaves a mess behind.
Anyone want to trade stories over a barrel of cider in {town}? I'll bring the old maps, and you bring the gossip.
Lag is no reason to rage-quit. Stand still, breathe, and let the server catch up. Works more often than you'd think.
Whoever keeps selling ale labeled as mead in the square, I can taste the difference from here, friend.
Good seasons never last long here. Enjoy the sunshine while the harvest is in and the roads are dry.
Bandits on the north road again. Someone should post patrol times before the new folks walk into them.
Grain prices in {town} doubled overnight. Either the harvest failed or somebody is hoarding. I'd like to know which.
{rival} has been undercutting every market for a week. Clever, but cheap wins never last.
I don't mind losing a fight. I mind losing it to a rule nobody bothered to explain.
Balance patch again and half the veterans are grumbling. Give it a month before anyone panics, as usual.
Back in the first war we had bandits too, only they had no horses. Tougher times, I suppose.
The {faction} toll on the trade road is steep. Not the end of the world, but I'd like the reasoning.
Honestly, the siege timers are what I'd fix first. Crew up, sit at the gate, and wait an hour. Dull.
Hauling a cart across the fens for half its old value. Ser, I've paid worse for less, but not much worse.
Nobody asked me, but caravan guards should not be easier to bribe than the bandits are to hire. Just saying.
Anyone with a sword and some patience, come join {my_faction} for the push on {fief}. We will feed you first.
Back in the first war, the best campaigns started with three honest volunteers and a warm fire. Still true.
Raid on {fief} forms at dawn. Bring your own rations, and I will show you the safe path through the reeds.
Looking for a few steady shields for a siege on {fief}. No glory hunters, please. We need people who hold the line.
Some of you asked how to get into a siege. Come to {my_faction}'s camp and I will walk you through it, no charge.
Our banners need more hands than they have. If you can march a day without complaining, we would be glad of you.
Honestly, {enemy_faction} will not hold {fief} forever. Join us before the next campaign and be part of the story.
Plenty of room in the ranks for anyone who wants to learn. Tell me what you can carry and we will find you a place.
Siege on {fief} is set for the new moon. Bring a shovel, a shield, and a bit of humility. Ser, that counts for a lot.
I have seen brave crews fall apart halfway through a raid. Come to {my_faction} with a steady head and we will not let that happen.
Ser, a fair price is one both sides grumble about a little. Anyone who leaves the table smiling was probably robbed.
Selling iron in {town} this week? Wait for the autumn caravans. Patience pays better than haste.
Someone just offered {gold} for a cart of salt in the square. Either a fool or a genius. Mind your purse, friends.
Prices in {town} climb every time the roads turn to mud. Stock up before the rains, not during them.
I paid {gold} for a warhorse years back and still call it a bargain. Quality is cheaper than regret.
Sell your surplus wool and grain, but keep a little back. Winter always arrives early somewhere.
Haggle all you like. Insulting the merchant's cousin in front of his stall is where I draw the line.
Charging {gold} for bread in a lean season is theft. Charging it in a good one is just greedy.
Check the old trade ledgers in {town} before you trust a price. Half the stalls here are older than most of us.
New traders, start small. A few coins of wool will teach you more than one big gamble ever could.
That field went the way it went. Next time bring more than enthusiasm, {player}.
Folks, a reminder: winning a skirmish does not make a war. I have seen plenty of both.
Lost {troop_count} men today. Some of you will call that a good trade. I do not.
Still standing on the same ground I held in the first war. Some things do not change.
Nobody is impressed by a lucky charge. Learn the terrain before you brag about it.
I will not repeat what I said to the last one who ran at my line like that.
Ask the old banners: the ones who rode too early always end up in the mud.
Keep your banners high, {player}. I will remember who was careless with my men.
Credit where it is due: that flank was clever. The rest of the plan was not.
Losing a field is cheap. Losing your head after is what ends a company. Pull yourself together.

whisper.text: You beat me fair on the day. Do not mistake that for forgiveness on the rest of it.
Your scouts were sharper than I gave them credit for. Remember that when we meet again.
I hold no grudge over the field. The insults you sent after, I noticed.
Plan your next raid around the river crossing. It has eaten better commanders than either of us.
Enjoy the win. Old wars taught me that victories this cheap rarely stay that way.
Do not bring that many banners to my border again unless you intend to pay for them.
You fight like someone who has read about battles and never buried anyone after one.
I will not chase you over a skirmish. Consider that a courtesy I am still deciding on.
That cavalry move was sharp. Your manners afterward were not. Work on one of those.
Keep this between us, but the next time you try a feint like that, I will be ready for it.

face.text: So you are the one who broke my left flank. Stand back from the horses, we are not finished talking.
I was hoping we would not meet like this. The field is behind us now, so let us be civil for a minute.
You have a good eye for a gap, I will give you that. Mind your rear though, friend. Men come back.
Look at the ground where your men are standing. That is where I buried the last captain who thought he had me.
No need for speeches. You won, I lost men. Tell me what you want from me and I will decide if it costs more.
I do not enjoy seeing my banners in the mud. That is the only thing I will say about today.
Your troops fought hard. Shame they were pointed the wrong way. That is a commander's fault, not a soldier's.
I am not going to bow or beg. Ride on, and we can revisit this at a time of my choosing.
Careful with that grin, {player}. Winning a field is a small thing when the fields keep coming.
We have met on the road now, which is more than I hoped for. Keep your distance and we will both live longer.

global.text: Field went to {player} today. Good ground choice, and we will see who holds it next season.
Counted our losses. Counted theirs too. Both sides lost something, which is how wars usually go.
Anyone travelling the eastern road, keep an eye out. The fighting moved faster than the messengers.
A reminder for everyone: the ones who keep records of each battle always outlast the ones who only remember them.
Hard day on the field. We are regrouping at the old waystation. Bring spare arrows if you come.
Fair play today, both sides. Nobody here needs a lecture on how a line breaks.
Tallied the field. The numbers look worse than they felt, which is true of most fields.
Still watching the roads. Whatever happened today, the grain carts still need escorts tomorrow.
Not going to pretend I saw that coming. Next time I will bring a longer view of the ridge.
Some of my men are asking whether to press on or retreat. I am asking the same question, quietly.

whisper.text: The field went your way. I will be watching how you handle the ground you took, not just the fight.
No hard feelings, I hope. You have a sharp line, and I have seen worse commanders keep their heads.
I need to know your intentions before the next muster. A straight answer would save us both trouble.
We lost the ridge today. That is the one thing I regret, and I will not blame you for taking what was open.
Send word if you want to talk terms. I would sooner trade prisoners than trade more blows this month.
Your scouts came in from the north. Mine did not. Let us compare notes sometime, when it suits.
Keep your distance until the dust settles. I am not in the mood to be seen losing gracefully.
That was a sound plan on your side. I am still working out whether it was luck or planning.
I have sent out parties to recover the wounded. If any of yours are near the ford, let them pass.
Our next meeting will be on better terms, or I will be surprised. Either way, I am keeping my notes.

face.text: You have the field, and I have the road home. Let us both be on our way before the sun turns.
Good ground choice. I should have anticipated the ridge. Do not expect me to make that mistake twice.
I am not here to argue the outcome. Tell me what you intend to do with the captured supplies and we can part.
Your archers were well placed. Mine were not. We can discuss that over a meal someday, if you want.
Stand easy. My men are tired and yours look no better. Let us not make tomorrow worse than today.
I have seen this ground change hands before. It tends to look different from the other side.
Winning here does not mean you own the valley. Keep that in mind when you pass through the villages.
We both have wounded to tend. I will see mine taken care of first, and then we can talk about the rest.
Your banners are up and mine are down for now. A fair trade for the day, I suppose.
No insult meant. You fought clean, I fought poorly, and the field remembers which was which.

global.text: Well played today, {player}. You made the ridge look easy, which means you did the hard part first.
Lost a field to {player} this afternoon. Honestly, I'd rather lose to someone who fights that clean.
Hats off to whoever trained the {player} company. Their line held better than most I've seen.
That was a hard-fought afternoon. Anyone who runs into {player} on the road, buy them a drink. They earned it.
Reminder for the new ones: you learn more from a loss to a fair opponent than from a win over a sloppy one.
Our side took a beating today. The ones who fought hardest were still standing at the end, which counts.
I'll be honest, that was the best-run field I've been on in seasons. Ser {player}, you have a gift.
The old banners would be proud of that charge. I'm not sure I'd have risked it, which says something.
Good match. We'll have another one soon, and I'll bring a better plan for the eastern hill.
Congratulations to the winners. Everybody who fought today should eat well tonight, win or lose.

whisper.text: Fought beautifully, {player}. I'll admit I had you worried for a moment on the left, and you did not blink.
Don't beat yourself up over the field. The ridge was yours from the start, and I should have seen it.
That cavalry push of yours was the best thing I've seen all season. Keep that instinct and you'll go far.
I owe you a drink for that match. Next time we meet, I'll buy and you can tell me how you did it.
The losses are mine to carry, not yours. Come find me when your men have rested, and we'll talk over the map.
Honest question: did you plan that flank, or did it just happen? Either way, it was beautiful to watch.
If you're thinking of pushing into the south, send word first. I'll lend you two of my best scouts.
Good win, and a better fight. Rest your horses before you go marching after the next thing.
I'd rather lose to you than to most. That's a compliment, in case it came out sour.
Between us, my captains couldn't stop talking about that charge all afternoon. You earned that.

face.text: Good to see you, {player}. That was a proper fight. My captains won't stop talking about your left flank. Sit, eat, we'll go over it.
You beat me clean today, and I'm still smiling about it. Tell me your secret before you leave for the coast.
Good to see you on your feet after that charge. Your men look fresh, and mine look like they need a month's sleep.
Lost the field to you, won the afternoon's conversation. Sit down, friend, the stew is still warm.
Ser {player}, a pleasure. Losing to a commander like you is easier to swallow than most wins I've had.
I've been thinking about your cavalry move since the field. I'd like to hear how you planned it, if you're willing.
Don't look so worried. I've lost worse afternoons and walked away with better friends. This is one of those.
There's no shame in being outplayed by someone who fights with that much care for their troops. Well done.
Come, let's walk the field together while the light's still good. I'll show you where I went wrong, and where you were lucky.
Good day's work, {player}. Before you ride off, take a little of the wine from my wagon. It's better than the field ale.

global.text: Third loss to the same banner. I'm starting to think someone here is keeping score just for me.
Back in the first war, a grudge like this ended in a truce or a grave. Pick one, please.
Lost to {player} yet again. Fine. I'll remember the route they took, and it won't happen a fourth time.
Another loss to {player}. Don't mistake luck for a plan, and don't expect me to cheer when it works.
Third defeat at the hands of {player}. I'm done being polite about it. Expect {troop_count} of my men at the next ford.
New folks, take note: the one who keeps beating you may not be the best. Just the most stubborn.
Some of you asked how to beat {player}. Honest answer: stop charging at the same gate.
Lost again to {player}. I'm not gloating about it, and I'm not forgiving it either.

whisper.text: Third loss, {player}. You're clever, I'll give you that, but cleverness wears thin after the third time.
Enjoy this one. I'm already planning the fourth meeting, and it won't go your way.
You keep finding my flank. Stop assuming I won't change my plan after the first two beatings.
I am not angry, just tired of watching my troops fall back from {player}'s banners.
Lost to you a third time, {player}. Rest well. I'll be awake thinking about the next field.
Don't mistake my silence for surrender. Your luck won't carry you past {troop_count} fresh recruits.
Third time. I respected you the first two. This time it's personal, and I don't forgive easily.
Your charge was good. Your patience was better. I'll learn it, and then you'll see me coming.

global.text: {player} has beaten me three times now. Not a rivalry yet, just a pattern worth noting.
Third fight, third loss. Anyone who faces {player} should expect a long afternoon.
Keep your food stocked and your scouts out, everyone. {player} has found the gap again.
Lost to {player} for the third time. I'd like a rematch someday, just not soon.
The fens taught me patience. {player} keeps reminding me it's a useful lesson.
Three losses to one banner is a lesson, and I've written it down so I stop repeating it.
Good fight, as always. Third time, though. Somebody should check the map for ghosts.
Everyone, watch how {player} times the charge. I've lost three times to it, so take notes.

whisper.text: Third loss, {player}. I'm not upset, just taking notes on your approach for next time.
That makes three defeats. You're consistent, {player}. I respect consistency even when it costs me.
No hard feelings, {player}. Three losses teach someone to stop charging the same gate.
{player}, I'd like to know how you keep reading my lines. Three times is no longer a coincidence.
Regroup before you sulk, {player}. I'm not sulking. I'm regrouping and counting my remaining troops.
We can talk it over with a meal sometime, {player}. Third fight, and I'd still like to know why.
Third defeat, {player}. Well played again. I'll bring {troop_count} troops next time and see if it helps.
You've beaten me three times now. Let's see if the fourth goes differently, {player}.

global.text: Third loss to {player} and honestly, the best fight I've had all season. Who else takes it this seriously?
Three defeats to {player}. Newer players, study that charge. It's the cleanest I've seen in ages.
Lost to {player} again. In the first war we'd have made a song of it. Glad that banner is on our side this season.
{player} beat me three times now. That's a rivalry worth keeping, the good kind.
Good fight again, {player}. Three losses and I still learned something new today.
Rest your troops, everyone. Third loss to {player}, and I'd still rather fight them than anyone.
Another clean win for {player}. Give them credit, everyone, and learn the formation.
Three losses to {player} and I've stopped counting it as a grudge. It's become a good habit.

whisper.text: Third loss, {player}, and I'm proud of you. Your timing keeps getting better.
Well fought again, {player}. Three defeats and you still make me want a rematch.
Don't let the streak sting, {player}. You've earned it, and I'd have lost it to anyone else.
We'll share a drink after the next battle, {player}. You owe me a rematch, and I owe you a better plan.
Three times now, {player}. You've taught me more than I taught any recruit this season.
Rebuild your line, {player}. Losing three times to you is nothing to be ashamed of.
Your flanking improved each time, {player}. Keep that up and I'll have to retire my old tricks.
Good game, {player}. Three losses and I'm still glad you're the one across the field.

global.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men today and still wants to talk about the 'fair' fight. Maybe go home and count them again.
Pleasant little skirmish. The field is ours now, and {gold} in spoils went to people who actually showed up.
Anyone else notice {player} runs straight at the enemy and hopes for the best? It worked out today. Barely.
Tip for the newcomers: if your banners are the first thing to break, don't bother charging next time.
Another field, another retreat for {player}. The fens must be getting crowded with people chasing that same banner.
I'd rather not gloat, but {troop_count} crossbowmen made a lovely line today. Who else wants a turn?
Some of us remember when {player} could hold a flank. Today it was more of a stroll.
The wall held, the gate didn't, and neither did {player}'s pride. Let's hope the next field offers more.
Wrote {player}'s name in the battle ledger under 'hard lessons.' Plenty of space left on that page.
Honest question: did anyone teach {player} that holding position means staying put? It got lost somewhere in the clash.

whisper.text: {player}, your line folded in the third minute. Next time, try holding the ground you started on.
Don't bother sending another messenger about a rematch. The results are already in the ledger.
Those {troop_count} men you lost were not cheap. Think about whether the next field is worth the coin.
I hear you're looking for revenge. Bring more than enthusiasm, because enthusiasm is what got your scouts killed.
We both know the flank broke first. I just wanted you to hear it from someone who saw it.
A word of warning: I don't offer second chances on the field. Learn from today or keep losing.
Your camp is still standing, which is more than I expected. Enjoy the quiet while it lasts.
Keep sending letters if it helps you sleep. My answer will still be the same banner at the ridge.
You fought well enough for the first hour. Shame about the second, since the first doesn't count for much here.
Ser, you are not the first to think their charge would break us. Most were less stubborn about admitting it.

face.text: {player}, you came all this way to stand in my shadow again? Bold. Let's see if your line holds better than your stories.
Another good field, and another one for the books. Step aside next time or the horses will be the ones who learn.
I won't pretend I enjoyed that. Your men fought hard, though you planned like someone who'd never lost a war.
Look at this, {player} still wants to talk. Speak fast, the wind is cold and I have {gold} worth of recruiting to finish.
Walk away while you can, {player}. There is no shame in running, only in coming back to the same ridge again.
You kept your banner up well. Pity it was pointed in the wrong direction the whole time.
Don't look at the dead like that. They chose their charge, and you chose to stand in their way. Rather different.
I've buried better captains than you, {player}, though not many. Keep practicing and maybe one day I'll remember your name.
A tidy win, friend. Now remember how this felt, because I plan to ask about it at the next muster.
Careful where you plant that flag. The last one who planted it there left with {troop_count} fewer men and a sore temper.

global.text: Field's clear. Anyone heading north should watch the fords, they're still soft from the rain.
{player} fought a clean battle today. Not my style, but I've seen worse from people with better numbers.
Good to see the roads quiet again. Everyone take a day to rest and tend your wounded.
Reminder for the new crowd: carry extra rations before you go anywhere near the marsh. Trust me on this.
The banners fell in an odd order today. Worth reviewing before the next muster.
Nothing personal to anyone out there, just a fair exchange of {troop_count} men on each side.
Did a few of you notice the scouts were late? Something to sort out before we march again.
Two armies met and one walked home lighter in the purse. Keep your own counsel and your coin close.
Not much to say about today except that the outcome matched the terrain. Make of that what you will.
Keep your eyes on the ridges. Whoever holds high ground at dusk usually decides what happens by morning.

whisper.text: {player}, the result is what it is. Keep your banner where people can see it, and we can talk when things settle.
The field went your way this time. Don't read too much into it, the wind shifted at the wrong moment.
Your archers held longer than I expected. Consider that before you assume the next battle will be easy.
Nothing to forgive or forget. Winning and losing are both just the way things go on this road.
If you're short on supplies, the market at the crossroads has grain. Prices were fair when I passed through.
I'd keep {gold} in reserve before hiring more sellswords. The last crew nearly sold you their own horses.
You made the ridge slower than it needed to be. Note that, and ask someone who has walked it.
Let's keep things civil. The roads are long, and I'd rather not spend my next winter counting graves.
You didn't embarrass yourself today. That's about as much praise as I hand out before supper.
Think about what your scouts told you before you committed. They usually know more than the banners do.

face.text: {player}. We fought, I won, and neither of us needs to pretend it was more than that. Ride on safely.
Your formation was tighter than I expected. Don't mistake that for a compliment, we both know the ground helped.
The horses are blown and so am I. Walk with me to the well, and we can speak about nothing for a while.
I don't hold grudges on the field, but I do keep a count. Yours is now one higher, for what it's worth.
Good that you came in person. Messages can be misread, and I'd rather look at your face when we disagree.
Water your mounts before you leave. The stream past the ridge runs dry by midsummer, and it's a long ride to the next one.
You're welcome to rest your men by the wagons. I expect nothing back, though a fair trade of news wouldn't hurt.
Hard to say whether today taught you anything. Some people need several fields before the lesson takes hold.
I've seen your banner before, {player}. Today it was higher on the hill, which is not nothing.
Whatever plans you're carrying, carry them somewhere quieter. Nobody here needs another skirmish before supper.

global.text: What a day for {player}! Held the center under pressure, and nobody else kept their nerve like that.
Good work, everyone who marched with {player} today. You kept the line together when it counted.
Newcomers, watch how {player} moved the flank. That's the lesson I'd want you carrying into your first real war.
{player} just taught a whole field how patience wins. Remember that, all of you, before you rush the next gate.
Proud of the ones who stood with {player} at dawn. We don't win battles alone, and today proved it.
I've seen many fights on this continent, and that was one of the cleaner ones. Thank you, {player}.
Fine work from {player} today. Get the wounded to the healers first and the victory songs can wait.
For those asking how the day went: {player} shaped it, and we all followed. Rest well, friends.
Ran into {player} after the fight and they gave {troop_count} men a proper send-off. That's leadership.
Good fight, and an even better one for {player}. Keep that spirit and this server will remember you.

whisper.text: {player}, that flank move was lovely. You had the timing right when most would have hesitated.
Well fought today. I'd like to hear how you read the ridge, because I missed it until it was too late.
Keep your head up. A good battle plan is still good even when it doesn't win, so don't let it weigh on you.
You led those {troop_count} soldiers well. Rest them tonight, and send me a note when you're ready to talk tactics.
Proud to have fought beside you, {player}. The next field is ours if you keep that composure.
If you want my advice on the next muster, stop by. I'd gladly trade a cup of wine for a good story.
Your discipline held when things went sideways. Not many people manage that, so remember you can.
Thank you for watching my left side today. I wouldn't have held it without you.
You did right by your men today. Spend a little of that {gold} on something nice for yourself, you've earned it.
Honest praise, {player}: that was clean work. Come find me when you want to swap notes on the terrain.

face.text: {player}! There you are. That was a fine day's work, and I'm glad we were on the same side of the ridge.
Sit down a moment, {player}. Your charge timing was sharp and the men noticed it. So did I.
I'd like to thank you properly for the flank today. Dinner's on me, and I don't take refusals.
Walk with me, {player}. I want to show you the fen crossing we used back in the first war. Saves a lot of trouble.
No need to apologise for the losses, friend. You made the right call with the ground you had, and I'd make it again.
Your scouts did excellent work. Remember to reward them, because the good ones are harder to keep than swords.
I'll tell any newcomer about today's fight. You held the line like someone who knows what it costs.
Rest your horses first, then we'll talk about the next muster. You have a steady hand, and we need steady hands.
Good to meet you in person, {player}. Your reputation on the road is well earned, and I say that as an old hand.
Whatever you do next, do it with that same calm. It serves you better than any banner ever will.
You fought well enough, but the first war taught me that a fine charge means little without a plan behind it.
I have watched your kind rise and fall on this road for years. Mostly fall, I'm afraid.
Your banners will be remembered the wrong way, I think. Eat your bread and keep your temper.
Hate me if it helps you sleep. I buried better enemies than you before the eastern bridge was rebuilt.
Shame. Another good blade wasted on a bad cause. Sit down before you make it worse.
Your purse still holds {gold} and you chose this road anyway. Remarkable, and not in a good way.
Every grudge on this server gets settled eventually. I just hope you are still breathing when yours comes due.
Tell {my_faction} I said nothing kind about you, {player}. They would not believe me anyway.
Your name came up at the old crossroads more than once, {player}. Let's see which story is true.
You are not the worst I have had sitting at this fire. Keep your hands where I can see them and we will manage.
The road to the coast is long. We can make it shorter if you answer a few questions honestly.
I have no quarrel with you yet. That can change quickly, so behave like someone with a future.
{my_faction} will want to know you are alive. I will decide whether that is worth the trouble.
A captive is both a burden and a bargain. Tell me what your purse holds and we will see what it buys.
Gold does not change the weather, but it does change how quickly people forget. Shall we talk about {gold}?
Eat, rest, and think about what you want from today. I have held worse prisoners and sent them home with boots.
Of all the riders who could have caught me, I am glad it was you, {player}. Sit, the fire is warm.
You fought like someone who listens to advice, which is rarer than you would think. Well done, truly.
No hard feelings from me. A good fight is a good fight, and yours was clean.
I remember the old tavern debts of the first war, and you paid yours in full. That counts for something.
Your ransom can wait a while. Let us share a meal first, it is hard to bargain on an empty stomach.
Had I been twenty years younger I would have hired you on the spot. Still, {gold} is a fine start for talks.
When you return to {my_faction}, tell them the captive was treated with respect. They will want to hear it.
Go easy on yourself for losing today. Every veteran here has lost a field or two, and most of us still laugh about it.
No alliance, {player}. I still remember how the last pact with your people ended, and so do the men who buried our dead.
You want my banner beside yours? Ask me again when the ground between our camps has stopped smelling of smoke.
Your offer is noted and refused. I have seen friendship from your corner before, and it always arrived with a knife behind it.
Pass. I would sooner ally with a wolf than with you, and at least a wolf is honest about who it bites.
Let me save you some time. The answer is no, the same as it was the last three times you asked, and it will be no tomorrow.
An alliance needs trust, and I have none to spare for {player}. Take your papers back to whoever sent you, and mind the road home.
Tempting, the way a fire is tempting in winter. I have been burned by fires like yours before, so no thank you.
Refused. If you want to prove yourself, do it on a field where I can watch. Words cost nothing, and yours have cost me plenty.
Thanks, but no. I keep my banners where they are, and I do not owe anyone an explanation for that.
An alliance is a rope with two ends, and I prefer to hold only my own. Thank you for asking, but no.
Not this season, {player}. My captains are stretched thin and my coin is spoken for. Perhaps the next time the roads are quieter.
I appreciate the offer. Pacts on this continent tend to outlive their usefulness, so I keep things simple and stand on my own.
No. Nothing personal. I have simply learned that a pact signed in good weather often breaks in bad.
Interesting proposal. I'll decline it for now, and we can both see how the wind blows before we tie our banners together.
Respectfully, no. I trust no one's word until their deeds have earned it, and yours are still being written.
I will pass on this one. Keep your forces where they serve you and I will keep mine where they serve me. Safe travels.
Ah, {player}, I wish I could say yes. My banner is tied up for now, but bring me the next proposal and I will listen properly.
You know I think well of you, so I will be honest. Not this time. Keep building your strength and we will talk again when my ranks are less stretched.
A fine offer, and it means something coming from you. I must decline, but you have my respect and my door stays open.
No alliance today, {player}, though I would fight beside you any day I could. Don't take it to heart. Old soldiers are cautious with their oaths.
Gracious of you to ask. I have been let down by promises before, which is why I count your word as worth more than most. Let's keep our friendship clean and our banners apart for now.
I have to say no, and it pains me a little. Stay safe out there, and send word if you need anything short of an oath.
Refusing you is the hardest thing I've done all week. It has nothing to do with doubting you. The timing is simply wrong.
Not now, {player}, but thank you for thinking of me first. Come find me when the roads are safer. I'd enjoy the company either way.
An alliance, then. We will see whether your word holds up as well as your sword does, {player}.
I accept. Do not make me regret it, and I will not make you regret it either.
Fine. Old soldiers learn that a signed bargain outlasts a grudge, so let's keep this one simple.
Agreed. Bring your banners to the eastern ford when the time comes and we shall talk tactics.
Very well. I have seen three alliances on this server collapse over a single cart of grain, so mind your supplies.
I accept. Keep your people out of my woods and we will get along fine.
Alliance accepted. I'll judge you by how you behave in the next skirmish, not by how sweetly you asked.
Yes, we can share the road. Just don't expect me to fight your quarrels with {rival} for you.
Gladly, {player}. Let's hope this one lasts longer than the last alliance I made on this server.
Of course I accept, friend. Come by the old watchtower tonight and we'll draw up the terms properly.
A good choice. I still remember when you first came through the gates, green as spring grass, and look at you now.
Accepted with pleasure. Between the two of us, {enemy_faction} will have a much harder winter.
Ha, I was hoping you'd ask. Bring your best scouts and I'll show you the safe paths through the marsh.
Done. You have never once let an ally down that I know of, and I don't intend to be the first to break faith.
Yes, gladly. Take this, a map of the crossings I drew back in the first war. Guard it well.
Accepted, and well done for asking. Plenty of new players would have been too proud to make the first move.
Let the road be wide enough for both of us, {player}. I have no wish to test your patience today.
I remember the last time you stood where you stand now. The ground there still has not forgotten it.
Walk on. Nothing you carry is worth the trouble it would cost you here.
I have buried braver men than you have met, and I did not enjoy one of those funerals. Go home.
Your banner is noted. Next time, bring a better reason to lift it in my direction.
No hard feelings, though I will admit I have a few soft ones saved up for later.
The mountain pass is long and you are not a patient traveler. Do not hurry on my account, but do not linger either.
You have chosen poorly in your allies, {player}. Mine are not so easily impressed, and neither am I.
Keep your distance from my supply wagons and we will get along fine. Cross that line and I will write it in the ledger.
Off you go. I have seen better schemes fall apart in a single afternoon, and I expect yours will be no different.
Good day, {player}. We are both headed the same way for now, so keep your blade sheathed and we shall get on.
Safe enough travels. I do not know your intentions yet, and I prefer to learn them before I make up my mind.
That is all for now. Watch the eastern bridge on your way, the river has been high and has taken a few careless wagons.
I have heard your name spoken in several places. Some good, some less so. Time will tell which were right.
Fair roads. We shall see each other again soon enough, one way or another, and I will judge then.
Nothing personal, {player}. I simply have a habit of letting the road decide who is worth talking to twice.
Mind the weather over the ridge. It turns quickly this time of year and I have no wish to pull anyone from the snow.
Go on, then. I will be watching the same roads you are, so do not be surprised if our paths cross once more.
Farewell for now. Keep to the marked trails and we will have no trouble between us that a cup of wine cannot fix.
Thank you for the conversation. I think it went about as well as these things ever do, which is to say it was adequate.
Safe roads, {player}. You have grown a great deal since I first saw you on the north wall. Keep that steadiness close.
It is a pleasure to see you on the road again. Come find me at the old inn when you have the time, I have stories to trade.
Remember to rest your horse before the climb. A tired animal makes for a poor escort and a worse excuse.
You fought well in the last skirmish, and I say that as someone who has been on the wrong end of far worse. Keep it up.
Go with my good wishes, for whatever a grizzled old veteran's wishes are worth. On a cold morning, they are worth a fair amount.
When the old wars come up in conversation, I will tell you how we managed it. Some of it may even be true.
Keep your flank covered and your temper cool, {player}. Those two habits have kept more of us alive than any sword.
You have a good head on your shoulders. Use it, and do not let the young ones talk you into anything foolish.
Until next time, {player}. The roads are kinder when good company travels them, and you are good company :)
Take care of yourself out there. Send word if you run into trouble, and I will come as fast as my old knees allow.
Stand aside, {player}. I have no quarrel with you today, and I would like to keep it that way.
Last time our roads crossed you left a cart burning behind you. I remember the smoke, if not the cart.
I have outlived three of your sort already. Each of them thought the road belonged to them. It never does.
Turn your banners around now and the ledger stays clean. Push on and I will write this one down in full.
There was a time I would have hung your colors from my tent pole. These days I only count the men behind you.
{player}, you have a reputation for running from fights you start. Let's see if that holds on this hill.
The first war taught me that grudges are cheap to carry and dear to bury. I'd rather not carry yours, but I will.
Your men look tired and your quartermaster looks worse. Go home before I am forced to make this a lesson.
{my_faction} has no interest in your coin or your boasts, only in the road beneath us. Step off it.
Spit on the ground all you like, {player}. The horses have seen worse and so have I.
Good day to you, {player}. Our paths cross, we both go our ways, and that is all I ask.
{persona} of {my_faction}, at your service, though I doubt either of us needs the other today.
Which way are you bound? We are heading east to the salt flats, if that matters to you.
Keep your distance and your hands off our wagons, and we will get along fine.
I don't know your banner well, {player}, so I'll take you for honest until you show me otherwise.
The road is wide enough for two parties, though some days it does not feel that way.
Nobody here has to fight today. Let's keep it that way and all go home with our purses intact.
Weather is turning. If you're heading north, you'd best move before the rain catches your column.
I have seen a hundred parties like yours on this road. You are not the first, and I expect you won't be the last.
We'll pass each other and say nothing. Sometimes that is the wisest way to spend an afternoon.
Good to see you, {player}. A familiar face on this cursed road is a gift. Walk with us a while if you like.
You held that ford well last season, {player}. Not many would have kept that line so long under such pressure.
Share our fire tonight. Good company is worth more than the wages of any hired sword :)
{my_faction} has always had a soft spot for those who keep their word. I suspect you are one of them.
Remember what I taught you about the tall grass and the long bridges. It will save your neck one day.
Back in the first war we would have called a truce for less than what you just did. Well played, {player}.
Go on, take the lead. I'll follow your banner for a mile and see whether your scouts are as sharp as rumor says.
Your name still carries weight at the old inns, {player}. Keep riding like that and the young ones will copy you.
Stay close to the river road tonight. I'll leave word at the waystation that you travel under my protection.
Whatever trouble you are in, bring it to my table. We have shared worse roads than this one.
Demanding my gold on the open road, {player}? The last traveler who tried that spent a week apologizing to the local magistrate.
Gold, you say. You would have {gold} from me? I have watched bolder threats die on this very road before lunch, so do try again.
In the first war I heard a hundred demands like this one. The ones who made them rarely lived long enough to make a second.
Surrender or pay, you say. Choose quickly, {player}, because my patience has outlasted more enemies than you have had birthdays.
A threat from a stranger on the road is just noise to me. Mind that the noise does not cost you your horse.
I will not hand over {gold} for the privilege of being left alive. Keep your coin and keep your distance, and we will both be better off.
You have the look of someone who learned bluster from a tavern song. Sing me a better one or step aside before the rain starts.
Bold words, {player}. Bold words are cheap, and I have a full purse and a long memory for those who insult me to my face.
Draw your blade if you must. I have buried better swordsmen than you in my time, and I still have time left for a cup of tea.
Your little ultimatum has been noted and filed beside the others. Next time, lead with respect and see how kindly the road treats you.
Ah, {player}. Threats first, names later? Fine. Tell me what you want, and I will tell you whether it is worth the walk.
Surrender, or pay {gold}. Those are the only two doors you have offered me, and neither is particularly wide.
I am not looking for a fight today, though I will not pretend I am afraid of one. Name your price, and we shall see.
Plenty of travelers have made demands at this crossing over the years. Most walked away richer in stories than in coin.
Strong words for a stranger. Let us both lower our voices and see if this can be settled before the horses get restless.
I have seen this exact standoff end three different ways. I would rather it ended with nobody's blood on the grass.
Gold is easy to lose and hard to earn back. Do you want to be paid, or do you want to be remembered as the one who started a brawl?
I do not owe you anything, {player}, but I do owe the road its peace. Make your case and I will listen while I decide.
You are not the first to stop me with a demand, and I suspect you will not be the last. Let us find out which kind you are.
No swords drawn yet, which I count in your favor. Speak plainly, and I will answer in kind.
Ah, {player}, you always did have a flair for the dramatic. Say what you need and we will sort it out over a warm fire.
Surrender or pay? Come now, you know I would give you the coin if you had asked nicely. Just ask nicely next time.
Put the blade away, my friend. I have watched you grow from a green fighter into someone worth standing beside.
That was a bold threat for a friend of mine. Bold, but unwise. Let us talk before the road decides for us both.
I have seen you hold your ground through worse than this, {player}. I suspect this is more bluster than real intent.
Pay {gold} to a friend? Never. But I will buy you a meal and hear what has troubled you enough to make you shout.
Save your ultimatums for the bandits, {player}. You know I have always had a soft spot for those who come to me honestly.
Good sport you are. Still, a threat from you makes me smile more than worry. Lead with a greeting next time, and we will get along.
Back in the first war, I learned that the best allies come from fierce tongues. You have a fierce tongue, so let us keep you on my side.
You have earned my respect many times over, so I will not take offense at this. Speak again when you have had a rest.
You want to trade with me now? I remember what your last deal cost the people who trusted you. Name your price, and I will count it twice.
{player}, a bargain from you is like a bridge made of wet straw. I will hear your offer, but I will not stand on it.
Trade, you say. Fine. Put {gold} on the table first, and we will see whether your word is worth more than the wind.
I have seen many proposals from you over the years, and most of them ended with someone else paying. Show me the terms and be quick.
Speak your offer, {player}. I will hear it, but do not expect me to smile while I do. Half the valley still owes me for your last promise.
Interesting. The one who once sold a broken cart to half of {town} is offering me a deal. I am almost flattered you remember my name.
Keep your hands where I can see them and your voice low. A trade with you is only safe when the scales are watched by someone who is not you.
I do not need your coin, {player}, and I do not need your friendship. But I will look at your offer, if only to see how far your nerve reaches.
A trade proposal. Good. Let me hear the terms, and I will tell you whether they are fair or merely clever.
Two hands, one table, and a fair price. That is all I ask. What is it you are offering?
Ser, I have traded in {town} since before the old wall fell, and I still read every contract twice. Go on, then.
My purse is not empty, but it is not generous either. Name a figure, and I will tell you if it leaves room for both of us.
Trading with strangers has taught me to keep my wallet close. Make your offer plainly and I will do the same.
Hmm. You have a proposal. I have a little time and a little patience. Spend neither carelessly.
If it is goods you want, bring them to the cart. If it is gold, tell me how much and what you intend to give in return.
I have heard worse ideas over a cup of ale and better ones from children. Let us see which kind yours is.
{player}! A trade between us is always welcome. Your offer is in good hands, so tell me what you have in mind.
Ah, you come to me with a proposal and a smile. That is how I like to start every good deal. Let us see what we can build.
I trust you, and that is worth more than any price on the table. Still, let us write the terms down so the old debts stay quiet.
Good timing, {player}. I was just thinking about how well our last exchange went. Make your offer and I will meet it halfway.
Bring your proposal to me, friend. Between honest people, a fair deal rarely needs more than a handshake and a little patience.
Offer {gold} and I will match it with supplies for your road. You have been good to the young ones here, and I remember it.
You have never once cheated me, {player}, so I will give your offer the honor it deserves. Speak freely.
Trade with you is a pleasure, and I say so as someone who has seen many bad bargains. Lay out your terms and we will shake on it.

global.text: Solid win today. Watch the flanks next time, the same mistake cost us at the ford in the first war.
Not bad for a morning's work. Let's see if the next one goes as cleanly.
Nice of the rearguard to show up at last. Let's see if it lasts past dinner.
Victories like this are easy to lose to greed. Take the win, then go home.
Lots of banners on the field today. Most will be forgotten by next month.
Could have ended faster if people kept their formation. Still, a win is a win.
{enemy_faction} will be back before the grain is in. We should be ready for that.
Reminder to everyone: collect your dead and count your arrows before logging off.

whisper.text: Your men held the ford well today. Don't let it go to your heads, the next one will be harder.
Decent work out there. I'll be watching how you handle the next push.
The win was real enough. Next time, check your supply lines before you march.
You fought alongside us today. Let's see if that's a habit or a fluke.
Took {troop_count} men through that field and didn't lose half. That's worth noting.
No need to thank me. Just keep your formation tight when we move out again.
Victory suits you well enough. Keep your head down and your ledger honest.
Heard your scouts were late. Get them sorted before the next engagement.

face.text: Well fought today. I'm not one for compliments, but your line did not break, and that counts.
We crossed paths on the field. Good that we were on the same side for once.
Nice to meet you properly. Winning together is a better introduction than most.
Keep your wounded close and your wagons closer. The road home is longer than the battle was.
I have seen a dozen victories like this one on this server. Each one ended with the same tired grin.
Don't stand so far off. We're on one side today, and that's rarer than you'd think.
The field is cleared. Take your men, rest them, and mind the mud on the road north.
Your banner did its job today. Let's hope the next rider who sees it knows what it means.

global.text: {player} held the center like it was nothing. Remember that day, it was a proper stand.
Proud to fight beside {player} today. Few here keep their heads that cool under fire.
Could not have asked for a better line than {player} and the crew on the east road.
Wins like this are why I still log on. Thank you, all of you who stayed the course.
{troop_count} strong and not a man broke. That is how the old veterans used to fight.
Kudos to {player} for pulling the wounded back. That kind of work doesn't get enough thanks.
If you're new and watched today's push, learn from it. Hold your ground and trust your flank.
Back in the first war we'd have sung about a day like this. Maybe we still should.

whisper.text: {player}, you fought like someone who has done this before. I noticed, and so will the others.
Thank you for covering my flank. I owe you a drink at the next muster.
Keep riding with us and you'll learn more in a month than most learn in a year.
That was a clean retreat when it mattered. Plenty of captains would have pushed on and lost it all.
If the road north gets rough, send word. I'll bring what supplies I can spare.
Your scouting saved us a bad afternoon. Remember that when you plan the next run.
I've watched you grow since the early days. Today was proof you've got the head for this.
Good to have you on this side of the field, {player}. Stay close and stay sharp.

face.text: {player}! Good to see you still standing. That charge on the left was something to watch.
You kept {troop_count} men alive out there. Few captains manage that. Sit with me a while before you ride.
Ah, a familiar face after the smoke clears. Take a moment. The horses need water and so do you.
On these roads, a sound retreat counts as much as a sound charge. You managed both today.
I'll be honest, I was worried about the center. You proved me wrong, and I'm glad to say so.
Next time we ride out together, let's plan the flank with you. Your instincts are sharper than most.
Come find me at the inn after dark. I'll buy the first round and tell you where the old ambushes were.
Good work today, friend. Keep that steady hand and you'll be leading your own banner before long.

global.text: {fief} is ours now. Garrison it properly tonight, because someone from {enemy_faction} will come asking for it back by morning.
Took {fief} without losing a banner. Reminds me of the first war, when we did it the hard way.
Easy advice for the new folks: a captured town is only yours once you've fed its people. Ask me how I know.
Well played, {my_faction}. Rest your troops and keep the gates shut, the roads are not safe yet.
Mind the granary in {fief}. Whoever holds the grain holds the peace, and I've seen that lesson cost more than a battle.
Some of {enemy_faction} will sulk about {fief} in global chat by supper. Let them. Sulking never retook a castle.
Not much to celebrate. We took {fief}, sure, but the real work starts now with the repairs and the tax rolls.
I won't say it twice: don't wander off alone near {fief} until the road is cleared. Patience keeps more people alive than swords do.
Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} is signed at last. The roads should be quieter for it.
Ser, a treaty is only as good as the next bored captain. Keep your banners up and your eyes open.
I have seen stranger endings than this, believe me. Yesterday's enemies are today's tired neighbors.
Stood at the old ford when the first war ended. Nobody cheered then either. Quiet peace lasts longer.
To everyone who spent last season raiding {faction}'s wagons, the ink is dry now. Please let it stay that way.
Traders, the tolls reopen with {faction} now. Stock up early before the crowds arrive.
No gloating from {my_faction} today. We signed because it was wise, not because we won the argument.
New folks, stay off the border roads for a few days. Fresh peace has sharp edges.
Sieging {fief} again. Back in the first war, that kind of pressure bred a long winter for everyone involved.
{player} has the walls surrounded. Fine. Just remember who else is watching this road.
Patience is a weapon too. We'll see who runs out of food at {fief} first.
Every siege at {fief} ends with someone counting their losses. I'd rather it not be my people this time.
I've watched {player} grow up on this server. Pressing {fief} like this is not a clever move.
The last crew that tried {fief} from that side lost half their banners. Just saying.
Drama is cheap. Siege engines are not. Choose which one you want to be known for, {player}.
Lift the siege before the rains come. The fens will swallow those camps whole.

whisper.text: {player}, I won't argue with your banners. But you're pressing {fief} with too few archers, and that will cost you.
Withdraw from {fief} while you still have your pride. Nobody here will think less of you for it.
I hold {fief} for a reason, {player}. Your scouts have been poking at the eastern gate for two days.
You won't find me shouting in global chat about this. But your camp at {fief} is a mistake, and I'd rather you learn it now.
Old hands know that sieges are won in the supply line. Check yours before you check the walls at {fief}.
Send your messenger back with terms if you want them. I'll hear them out, though I'm not feeling generous.
{player}, your quarrel is with my garrison, and my garrison doesn't scare easily. Take a breath.
Lose a few men here and you'll be licking your wounds for a month. Trust me, I've been there.

global.text: Siege at {fief} going on. Keep your food stocked, folks, the roads are getting long this season.
{player} has the gate at {fief} under pressure. Time will tell whether it was worth the coin.
Seen plenty of sieges on this continent. Most are over before the cooks run out of bread.
Watching the lines form around {fief} this morning. Quiet fight so far, which I prefer.
Good luck to both sides at {fief}. Keep the wounded away from the road, that's all I ask.
Whatever happens at {fief}, I'll be standing with the traders who have to cross afterwards.
Not my war, not my walls. Still, I'll mention that {fief} has a poor well for a long siege.
Siege at {fief} started this morning. Let's hope the smiths on both sides stay busy with plowshares.

whisper.text: {player}, if you're after a fair fight at {fief}, you'll get one from me. Just don't bring the fens into it.
Heard you've set up outside {fief}. Mind the marsh to the south, the ground there sucks boots off.
I won't take sides at {fief}, {player}. But if you need a ford map or a supply tip, ask quietly.
Your siege is your business. My only advice is to rotate your men before they start fighting each other.
Hold your ground if you must, but don't burn the mill outside {fief}. The whole valley eats from it.
Some sieges are won by patience, others by a good cook. Think about which one you're playing.
Ser {player}, I'm neither for nor against you here. Just keep your banners clear of the trade road.
Think about the next ten years, {player}, not just the next ten days. Good reputations outlast walls.

global.text: {player} lost {troop_count} men and still wants to lecture everyone on tactics? Save it for the fens, ser.
Took {player} long enough to learn that a lone banner is just a target. Ask the old hands if you need reminders.
Lost {troop_count} troops and blamed the weather. Every veteran here has heard that excuse before, {player}.
Some of us warned {player} about marching without scouts. Pride is expensive, and it just cost {troop_count} soldiers.
Crushing loss, {player}. Hard to feel sorry when the same mistake gets made every season on this server.
Mourning isn't my habit, {player}, but that river crossing was never going to end well.
{player} rode out with {troop_count} men and came back with a fraction. Next time, listen before charging.
Bad day for {player}. Those who keep marching into the same trap will keep losing, so think it through.

whisper.text: Your {troop_count} men deserved better orders, {player}. Lead them differently next time or stop leading at all.
I won't waste sympathy on you, {player}. Go count what survived and learn from what didn't.
Keep your distance from my fiefs for a while, {player}. You've lost enough troops to be a nuisance.
Losing {troop_count} soldiers is a lesson, not a tragedy. I'd still rather you learned it somewhere else.
Your retreat was messy, {player}. Next time, pull back before the line breaks, not after.
Spare me the tearful messages. You made the call, you pay for it, and it cost {troop_count} lives.
Don't expect help from me while you sulk, {player}. Rebuild on your own, or don't rebuild at all.
Pride got you into that mess. Admit it to yourself at least, since nobody else here will bother.

global.text: {player} took a hard hit today. Happens to the best of us, so let's see what comes out of the ashes.
Heard {troop_count} soldiers didn't make it back from that field. Hope {player} keeps the rest alive.
A rough day for {player}. Keep the company close and don't chase the enemy without a plan.
A standing army is only as strong as its scouts. Ask around before the next campaign.
Losses like that are part of the game. {player} will be back on the roads soon enough, I expect.
Would have called that battle a draw if the numbers hadn't gone so lopsided. Heavy price for {player}.
Plenty of banners were broken out there today. Keep your head, {player}, and your supplies full.
A defeat like that teaches more than any victory. Let's see what {player} makes of it.

whisper.text: Heard about the battle, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men is hard, but the campaign isn't over yet.
Your army took a beating. Recruit wherever it's cheap and stick to the roads you know are safe.
Sorry about the loss, {player}. If you want to compare notes on that field, I'm around.
{troop_count} troops gone is a bad morning. Rest them before you move again, or they'll desert you.
No need to panic, {player}. Gather what remains and count your supplies before choosing a route.
That fight went badly. Write down what went wrong while it's fresh, it'll save you trouble later.
Hard luck, {player}. Armies recover, reputations take longer, so be careful who you ride with.
Your men fought well before the line broke. Keep that in mind when you rebuild the company.

global.text: Brutal fight for {player} today. Losing {troop_count} men hurts, but I've seen worse come back stronger.
Stand up straight, {player}. One bad field doesn't undo a good campaign. Rebuild and we'll see you on the roads.
Hard day for {player}, and the company knows it. Anyone with spare grain, help them get back on their feet.
That was a rough one, {player}. Take the lesson, keep your head up, and don't let it stop you.
Lost {troop_count} to that ambush? Let's make sure {player} isn't walking back alone. Who has spare rations?
Few of us came through that field clean. {player}, you fought harder than most, and that counts for something.
Tough breaks for {player}. Keep the veterans close, they've all crawled out of a ditch like this before.
Rebuilding after a defeat like that is no shame. Good soldiers carried {player} through it, and they'll do it again.

whisper.text: I'm sorry about your losses, {player}. You held the line longer than most would have. Rest up.
{troop_count} men is a painful number, ser. Come find me if you want help planning the rebuild.
That loss will weigh on you a while, {player}. When you're ready, I'll help you plan the next march.
You kept more of your company alive than the field deserved, {player}. Be proud of that much.
Take a few days off, {player}. The men will be ready to march again once you've had some sleep.
I've lost more armies than I can count, {player}. The trick is coming back with a plan, not anger.
If you need a quiet place to regroup, my camp's open. Bring your remaining troops and we'll sort them out.
Losing that many soldiers hurts, {player}. Write down what you'd do differently. I did the same once.

global.text: Running from the field again, {player}? Some things never change on this server.
I remember when the first war still had people standing their ground. Those days seem gone.
Retreat is a fine tactic, as long as you don't call it a victory afterward.
Half the veterans here have turned tail once or twice. Doesn't make it any less noticeable.
Ran off before the first clash. Bold of you to leave your own troops to hold the line.
Nobody's counting the scattered riders, but the ones who stayed will remember who left them.
Fast legs, I'll grant that. Shame the banners didn't keep up.
Quite the disappearing act. Try not to lose the road home too.
Some of us came to fight. Others came to watch the dust settle. Makes the record easy to read.
Cut and run before contact. The old hands in this chat have seen that before, and they remember it.

whisper.text: {player}, a retreat before the line even formed is not a plan. Think about what your riders saw.
I won't pretend that was a fight. You left the field before the first arrow flew.
You want my advice? Stop running and pick a battle you can actually finish.
Chasing you across the map would waste my afternoon. Consider yourself lucky, for now.
That was a sorry exit, {player}. Your company deserved a better captain than that.
Next time you turn tail, at least leave the banners behind. They were never yours to carry off.
I've seen better courage in a sheep pen. Keep your scouts closer next time.
No hard feelings, but I'd rethink the next engagement before your horses get tired.
Running is an honest choice. Just don't expect the same courtesy from the men who stayed.
You scattered the moment the drums started. Work on your nerve before you try the next border.

global.text: Saw {player}'s party break off before the clash. Could be wisdom, could be bad timing.
Fighting withdrawals are underrated. Plenty of good captains have used one.
Tactical retreat or a rout? The map will tell us in a day or two.
Ran from the field today. Whatever the reason, nobody here needs the details.
Some folks charge in, some fall back. Both have their place when the terrain is wrong.
Keep an eye on {player}'s riders. Nothing wrong with withdrawing early, but it's worth noting.
I've retreated before a bad fight myself, back when this server was younger. Lived to tell it.
The fens are no place to make a stand with a tired company. Sensible move, I suppose.
No judgment yet. Let's see if the retreat was wise or just lucky.
A scattered line means a long night of regrouping. Hope the troops are fed.

whisper.text: {player}, I saw your party break off before the clash. Was it the terrain or the numbers?
Pulling back is no shame if you live to fight another day. Just don't make it a habit.
Your riders looked spread thin out there. Pick a place to regroup where the ground favors you.
If the enemy was too strong, a retreat was wise. If not, you'll want to figure out why.
Retreating from a fight tells the whole server a little about you. Make sure it says what you intend.
Good call getting out before the lines met, provided your scouts were right about the numbers.
Regroup and rest your horses. Nobody's chasing you tonight, as far as I can tell.
I'd like to hear what you saw before you turned around. Two heads are better than one on the road.
Withdrawing is a skill, {player}. Most people only learn it after they lose a company.
Stay clear of the river crossings for a while. Scouts reported trouble moving in that direction.

global.text: Good call pulling back, {player}. Living to fight another day beats a bad trade every time.
{player} knows when the odds are wrong. Wise captain, and the server needs more of those.
Smart withdrawal today. Your people will thank you for not feeding them to the lines.
Falling back from that field was the right move. Plenty of veterans would have stayed and lost the lot.
Retreat with your banners held high is still a retreat worth respect. Well done, {player}.
Some would call that cowardice. I call it keeping your troops alive. Good judgment.
I've made that same retreat more than once. Never regretted it, and neither should {player}.
Tactical withdrawal, clean and quick. Exactly what the new folks should learn from watching.
Nobody lost a company today thanks to {player}'s sense. Keep that instinct sharp.
Quick feet and a clear head saved a lot of trouble out there. Nicely handled.

whisper.text: {player}, that was a sensible withdrawal. The field was not yours to win today, and you knew it.
You kept your riders intact, which is more than most would manage in that spot. Well judged.
Don't let anyone shame you for falling back. Your troops will be fighting again next week because of it.
I was watching from the ridge. That retreat was clean, and the men were in good order.
Pull back, rest, and restock. Once your company's fed, the next fight will go much better for you.
Good instincts today, {player}. The line you avoided would have cost you a lot of good men.
Take the lesson from this one. Knowing when to leave is as valuable as knowing when to charge.
Lost ground is easy to earn back. Your company is the thing that matters, and you kept it whole.
If you want a second opinion on the map before the next move, I'm happy to look it over with you.
That was a proper retreat, {player}. Keep your banners up and your wits about you on the road.

global.text: {fief} handed out like a tavern tab. Fine. Let's see how long it stays in one pair of hands this time.
Back in the first war, a fief that came easy usually left just as easy. I'll be watching {fief} with interest.
Some of us spent years earning a keep. Others got one from a single audience. Enjoy the walls, {player}.
Could be a fine gift for {player}. Could also be a fine target. Hope the garrison is paid up.
Lord-granted fiefs are nice until the neighbors start asking why. Expect questions from {fief}'s borders soon.
Ruler's favorites get a castle and a lot of enemies. Hope {player} brought spare soldiers.

whisper.text: {player}, I don't say this to be unkind, but {fief} came too easy. Easy things get watched closely here.
Congratulations on {fief}. I'll keep my opinion of the grant to myself for now, but I have one.
Don't mistake a title for respect. Respect comes from the people who've held a border for years.
You got {fief} without a single siege. I'd still like to see you hold it through one before I clap.
If you're expecting me to smile at the grant, you'll be waiting a while. Prove the ruler right, {player}.
Enjoy the new walls. I'll be the one counting the days before the first raid lands on {fief}.

global.text: {fief} changed hands by royal decree today. Interesting timing. Everyone keep an eye on the roads.
A new holder for {fief}. I've seen this movie before, and it ended with three rebellions and a fire.
Good to see the ruler rewarding someone. Let's see whether the rest of us get any notice first.
Fiefs are only as good as the people willing to defend them. Time will show what {player} is made of.
Hm. {fief} under new management. I'll reserve judgment until the first harvest comes in.
Whoever holds {fief} now, I hope they keep the mill running. Nothing sours a region like empty bread ovens.

whisper.text: {player}, you've got {fief} now. Keep the granary full before anyone starts testing the walls.
I'm not sure whether to congratulate you or pity you. Ask me again after the first winter at {fief}.
The ruler's favor is a good start. Keeping the people of {fief} happy is the harder job.
Welcome to the responsibility side of things. The tavern sweets are much nicer than the tax ledgers.
If you want advice on {fief}, ask before you rebuild anything. I learned that one with a collapsed wall.
Gained a castle, and now you have to answer every rider who asks about it. Get used to that, {player}.

global.text: Well earned, {player}. {fief} is in good hands, and I'll say so to anyone who asks.
Our ruler finally got one right. {fief} deserves someone who shows up early and stays late.
Good to see {player} getting a proper reward. The old hands have been waiting on this for a while.
Raise a cup to the new holder of {fief}. Pay the garrison first and the rest will follow.
The best grants go to people who already act like lords. Congratulations on {fief}, {player}.
I remember the first time I was handed a fief. Tired, happy, and worried about the roof. Enjoy it, {player}.

whisper.text: Congratulations on {fief}, {player}. Send word if you want me to look over the defenses sometime.
You earned that grant. Don't let the first rush of pride make you ignore the stores, though.
Proud of you for this one. Hold {fief} well and I'll tell the story at the tavern for years.
If the ruler's stewards give you trouble over {fief}, come find me. I've sorted that mess before.
New holder of {fief}, eh? Remember, the best lords I've known spent more time on roads than in halls.
Keep your head down at {fief} for a month and let the people see you work. The title will mean more then.

global.text: Swore to {my_faction} and already picking fights with the old hands. Bold start, {player}. We'll see how long it lasts.
Another oath, another face on the walls. I remember the first war, and so should you. Keep your word this time.
Ser {player}, I'll reserve judgment until this oath has some proof behind it. Don't make me regret the vouching.
Welcome to {my_faction}, {player}. Mind the ledger. We keep track of who burns the granaries.
Sworn in and smiling already. The fens remember who sold out the last banner, and so do I.
I've buried plenty of oath-breakers, {player}. Take your vow seriously, because the rest of us will.

whisper.text: {player}, I didn't ask for you in my ranks. Prove the oath was worth the ink and we can talk.
Don't expect a warm bed or a warm welcome. You'll earn both or you won't, and I'll be watching.
Keep your distance from my quartermaster until I've seen your ledgers. Consider this a courtesy.
The ones who swore to {my_faction} before you didn't last. Try not to be the next one I write off.
Rough sort of oath to take this late, {player}. I hope you know what you're signing up for.
If you're here to climb, climb quietly. I've no patience for ambition wearing a fresh cloak.

global.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Fine. Oaths are cheap until the weather turns.
New banner on the roster. Let's see who holds the line when the first siege comes up.
Another name in the book. Good luck to them, and a sharper eye for the fens than most.
Interesting timing for an oath. Hope it wasn't made in a tavern at midnight.
We take all comers, but we don't vouch for them yet. Time will tell whose word holds.
Ser {player} is ours now. Nothing changes for the rest of you, so carry on.

whisper.text: {player}, you're on the muster list now. Read the standing orders before you wander off anywhere.
Welcome to {my_faction}. I don't know you well yet, so I'll keep my opinions to myself.
Your oath is on record. Stay out of the eastern passes until you know the ground.
Nothing personal, but we'll see what kind of soldier you are before I lend you anything.
Pleasant enough to meet you, {player}. Keep your head down for a week and you'll be fine.
Ask your questions here, not in open chat. Most of them already have answers buried in the logs.

global.text: Glad to have {player} under the banner. Good oath, good company, and a warm welcome from all of us.
A solid recruit joins {my_faction} today. Newcomers, give {player} some room and some advice.
Good to see {player} sworn in. {my_faction} has plenty of honest hands, and now there's one more.
Raise a cup for {player}, our newest. The first war taught me that loyal folk make the best wall.
Oath taken, banner raised. {player}, you've made a fine choice, and {my_faction} is better for it.
Welcome aboard, {player}. Ask any veteran here and they'll tell you the same: you chose well.

whisper.text: Glad you came to {my_faction}, {player}. Pack a spare saddle and a full purse before you ride out; the roads are rough.
Well sworn, {player}. Come find me at the hall and I'll show you the quiet paths I used when I started.
You made a good call today. Keep your head, keep your friends close, and you'll go far here.
I'll look out for you while you find your feet, {player}. Ask me anything, no question is too small.
Proud to have you on the roster. Rest your horse tonight, we have plenty of work tomorrow.
Welcome, {player}. If the early skirmishes go badly, remember I lost more than I won in my first season and still stayed.

global.text: {player} switched colors and expected nobody to notice. Everyone noticed.
Some folks trade their banner for a warmer hearth. Enjoy the new roof, {player}.
Back in the first war, deserters got a rope. Today they get a long memory.
{faction} may welcome a turncoat, but they will count every shield you carry.
Loyalty is a small coin, {player}. Some of us still keep ours in a tight purse.
Still waiting for {player} to explain the ride over to {faction}. I have time, and a long memory.

whisper.text: {player}, you left {my_faction} at the gate and walked off smiling. Don't expect a warm welcome next time.
Heard you are wearing {faction}'s colors now. Wear them well, because we will remember this face.
Every deserter thinks the grass is greener. Mostly it is just more mud, {player}.
You know what the old hands say about turncoats? They make poor company in a siege.
No hard feelings? I'd say plenty of hard feelings. Keep your distance from our walls.
Your name is still on our rolls, {player}. We haven't crossed it out yet, and we won't forget why.

global.text: {player} moved to {faction} this week. Fine. Let's see how long the coin lasts.
Plenty of people change banners. The ones who last are the ones who stay put.
Saw {player}'s new tabard at the crossroads. Hope the cloth is warmer than our hall was.
Doors open both ways here. Just don't be surprised when people remember which way you walked.
The fens don't care what color you fly, {my_faction} included. Mind your footing, {player}.
Switching flags is allowed on this server. Whether it's wise is a question I'll leave to time.

whisper.text: {player}, you're free to choose your flag. I'd just ask you to think about who you stand beside.
Your choice to join {faction} is your own. Don't ask me to pretend I'm not disappointed, though.
Think it through before you pledge fully. Half-hearted oaths are the ones that break in a siege.
If {faction} treats you well, good for you. If not, our gates remain, for now.
Some turn coats for a better purse, others for a better cause. Which one are you, {player}?
I won't hold a grudge over a banner. I will remember how you handled the parting, though.

global.text: {player} took the road to {faction}. We'll miss the steady hand, but no grudges from me.
Shame to lose {player} from our ranks. Still, a good soldier is a good soldier wherever they stand.
Parting ways with {player} stings a bit. The old hall will still have a seat for them.
Don't let anyone tell you that leaving was dishonest, {player}. It was a hard choice, and you made it openly.
Remember the first war? We learned that friends sometimes wear different colors and still hold the line.
Good luck to {player} over at {faction}. Honor the oaths you make there, and we'll cheer you on.

whisper.text: {player}, I'm sorry to see you go, but I understand the reasons. Come find me if you need advice.
You always carried yourself well in our ranks. I expect the same standard under {faction}'s banner.
No hard feelings from this old hand. You earned your place with honest work, and that won't vanish.
If {faction} asks too much of you, come back and talk. Our door doesn't lock on friends.
Leaving was a bold move, {player}. Make sure it was the right one, and then give it everything.
I'll be watching the next big battle, {player}. Fight like you did for us, and you'll be fine. :)

global.text: Burned {village} to the ground and called it a raid. Enjoy the reputation, {player}. It won't be a long one.
Another village gone to smoke. Half this server would rather trade than torch. Not that you'd know, {player}.
{village} had a decent well and a better bakery. Shame. Hope the loot was worth the damn smoke.
Raiding a village teaches nothing but how to hold a torch. Took me years to figure that out.
Somebody tell {player} that arson isn't a trade skill. Or maybe it is. Hard to tell anymore.
We'll be remembering the ashes of {village} when you come knocking next. Keep your gates shut, {player}.
Heads up, new folks. {player} burns villages for sport. Keep your stores behind walls.
Back in the first war, we'd have hanged someone for that. Times change, I suppose. Not always for the better.

whisper.text: {player}, you burned {village}. I'm not going to pretend I'm surprised. Next time, come talk to me first.
That was a cruel way to spend an evening, {player}. I hope it felt good, because it won't last.
I've watched you for weeks, {player}. Raiding {village} was the sloppy kind of bold. Don't mistake it for smart.
Those people had nothing to do with your quarrel. Point the next fight at soldiers, not farmers.
You'll find no welcome at the next village over. Word travels faster than your horse, {player}.
I'll be sending the rebuild crew to {village} tomorrow. You won't be invited to help.
Don't bother with an apology. Ashes don't take well to them, and neither do the people who lost homes.
Enjoy the spoils while they last, {player}. I'm keeping a ledger, and this one's on your name.

global.text: {village} burned last night. Could have been anyone with a torch, and the roads are long enough for that.
Raids are part of this server, I suppose. Doesn't make the smoke any sweeter to look at.
Saw {player} riding out of {village} with a wagon. Not my business, though I'll be keeping an eye out.
Whatever happened at {village}, I'd rather see the next fight on a battlefield than in the fields.
Quiet week on the roads, then {village} goes up in smoke. Funny how that goes.
