Keep your food stocked and your walls up, new folks. The raiders are out again.
Didn't really expect {player} to take that road. Oh well. Everyone has their own reasons.
Let's not turn {village} into a feud. Ashes heal slower than people think.

whisper.text: {player}, that raid on {village} was noticed. I'm not your enemy yet, so let's keep it that way.
I don't know your reasons, {player}, but if you want to talk terms, I'll listen before I swing.
If you're looking for a quiet trade route, {village} is no longer the place to ask for one.
Mistakes happen on the road. Owning them afterward is what sets people apart around here.
Not going to lecture you. Just know the folks of {village} are watching who passes by now.
You might find a fair deal with the next village over. Ask around before you pick a side.
No hard feelings, yet. I'd rather not be counted among the people you raid, {player}.
We'll see how the next month goes. Some folks bounce back from a bad night, and some don't.

global.text: {player} has climbed fast, but I've watched a dozen names rise and fall since the first war. Keep your feet on the ground.
Renown is a fine thing, {player}. It also makes you an easy target. I'd sooner see you earn respect than demand it.
Plenty of names got loud on this server before {player}. Most of them are gone now. Let's see how this one holds up.
I don't much care for the way {player} talks about the lesser houses. Reputation cuts both ways, and so does a sharp tongue.
{player} is making a name, and I'd rather it be a name people trust. Right now that trust is thin.
Hm. {player} stacks up victories and forgets who helped carry them. Old servers remember that sort of thing, too.
{player} is building a reputation quickly. Time will show whether it's earned or just loud.
Saw {player}'s name on the board again today. Plenty of reputations pass through here. We'll see which kind this is.
Good for {player}, I suppose. Renown is cheap until someone has to defend it on a bad night.
New names rise every season. {player} is doing well so far, though the fens are patient with everyone.
I've nothing against {player}. I've simply learned not to judge a name by how fast it climbs.
Renown brings visitors, and visitors bring trouble. Keep an eye on your supplies, {player}, and your back.
{player} has come a long way in a short time. Proud to see a newer player earn a name this honestly.
Well played, {player}. Half of the old hands here wouldn't have handled that last siege half as well.
If you need a steady hand on the road, {player}, you know where to find me. Glad the server's getting to know you.
Quite the rise, {player}. Remember the ones who helped you get here. Reputation fades fast without friends.
I've said it before and I'll say it again: {player} fights clean and lends a hand. That's what makes a name last.
Good to see {player} recognized at last. Enjoy it, and then go back to teaching the new folks the ropes.
{fief} has changed hands on me before. It will change back. Enjoy the walls while they last.
Taking {fief} from us was a fair move, {player}. Keeping it is the harder part, and I have watched plenty fail at that.
Old hands in this realm remember who held {fief} first. Don't mistake a captured gate for a won war.
Congratulations on {fief}, I suppose. The garrison was thin, and everyone can see it from the road.
Some of us still have old maps of {fief}, down to every ditch and back gate. Enjoy the view from the wall.
I won't waste breath sulking. Hold {fief} for a season, then we can talk about who really won.

whisper.text: That was a clean capture, {player}. I'm still not pleased about it, and I won't pretend otherwise.
You took {fief} with a sharp plan. Don't expect me to thank you for the lesson.
Keep your eyes on the east road. Anyone who takes a town like that will come looking for the next one.
I'll be watching how you run {fief} now. Ruling a place is harder than storming it, ser.
I'll keep my words civil in public. In private, I would still like {fief} back. Just so we're clear.
Hold it well and you've earned my respect. Lose it the way I did and you'll learn what I learned.

global.text: {fief} changed flags again. Fine by me, so long as the granary still feeds the villagers.
Whoever holds {fief} this week, the roads are still muddy and the taxes are still too high.
Took {fief} clean, by the look of the reports. Wary folk will be checking their gates tonight.
New lords in {fief} mean new rules at the market. Read the posted notices before you trade there.
Hard to say whether {fief} gains or loses from this. Time usually sorts that out.
Ser {player}, I'll take your word on the siege. Keep the bridge repaired and we'll get along.

whisper.text: Took {fief}, I hear. Let's not make this a feud. Trade routes still matter to both of us.
I have no quarrel with the capture itself. Just keep the caravans moving through {fief} safely.
Congrats on {fief}. If you need supplies, I can point you to a fair price.
Watch the granary in {fief}. The last garrison left it nearly empty, and nobody wrote that down.
I'm not sure yet whether you're a neighbor worth having. Prove it over the next few weeks.
Strong move on {fief}. I'll keep my distance until I know which way you intend to lean.

global.text: {player} has a long winning streak now. Streaks end, and they usually end at the worst possible moment.
Another win for {player}. I remember when a run like this made the whole server nervous. It passed. It always does.
Nobody on this server is impressed by a streak yet. Ask me again after the next siege.
Lucky timing and a full purse can carry anyone through a few fights. Let's see who's still standing in a month.
I've watched three champions rise and fall here. Being on top is the quickest way to get a line of people hoping you trip.
Some of you are cheering {player} as if this were a new age of heroes. Wins come cheap when the other side is distracted.
Every streak I've seen was built on fights nobody else bothered to show up for. Remember that before crowning anyone.
I don't mind {player} winning. I mind how the winning gets talked about. Keep the boasting short.

whisper.text: Enjoying the streak, {player}? Enjoy it while the roads are quiet. They get busy fast once people start planning.
Your run of wins has caught the attention of people who don't forget. I'd watch your back for a while.
I won't congratulate you. Winning this often makes people careless, and careless people end up in my ledger.
Every streak ends in a loss. I'd rather yours ended somewhere other than in front of my banners.
You've been lucky with your timing, {player}. Luck is a poor thing to bet a whole fief on.
Pride looks good on the scoreboard. It looks less good when the supply wagons stop arriving.
Don't mistake a few wins for a reputation. Reputations take years to build and an afternoon to lose.
I'll keep my distance for now. When someone who wins this much finally picks a fight with me, I'll be ready.

global.text: {player} is on a real run now. Good. This server could use a fight that doesn't end in arguments.
Interesting stretch of wins from {player}. I'll wait and see how the next few weeks go before forming an opinion.
Many wins in a row draw attention. Attention brings envoys, scouts and the occasional bad idea. Plan for all three.
A streak like this belongs in the server ledgers, if nothing else. Keep your logs, folks.
Strong run, {player}. Remember that the people you beat today may be the ones writing letters tomorrow.
The map looks different after a run like that. Borders move, alliances shift, and everyone starts counting.
Credit where it's due, {player} has been winning steadily. Whether it lasts depends on what happens between battles.
Long streaks tend to bring out two kinds of people: those who want to learn from them and those who want to copy them.

whisper.text: Your recent run has people talking, {player}. Keep an eye on who talks the loudest.
Quite a streak. If you want advice from someone who has watched a few of these, keep your sword hand free for surprises.
I'm not sure yet whether you're a rising name or a passing one. Ask me again when the streak breaks.
Don't let the praise go to your head, and don't let the critics get under your skin. Both pass quickly.
Good numbers, {player}. Keep a written record of your battles. It helps when people start misremembering.
If anyone offers to fight beside you for a share of the glory, have them write down the terms first.
Winning this often means favors will be asked of you soon. Decide now which ones you'll refuse.
I wouldn't change how you fight just yet. I'd only change who you let flatter you.

global.text: {player} has been winning steadily and doing it cleanly. That's the kind of play newcomers should study.
Proud of how {player} has been fighting lately. Streaks are rare, and this one was earned in the open.
Seeing {player} string wins together reminds me why I still log in every evening. Keep it up, friend.
A few more of these and the younger players will start copying {player}'s formations. That's a fine legacy.
Nice run, {player}. The fiefs you took were defended by people who knew what they were doing, too.
Some streaks fade fast. This one looks sturdy. Good discipline on the field has a way of lasting.
Congratulations to {player} on the streak. Share your method with the newer folks when you get the chance.
If the server ever writes a history of its good fights, {player} will already have a whole chapter.

whisper.text: Take a day away from the field before the next fight, {player}. Even the best need to step back for a while.
Your last few battles have been a pleasure to watch, {player}. Thank you for fighting with such care.
Don't let the streak go to your head. Keep helping newcomers the way you have, and the wins will mean more.
I'm proud to have you on this server, {player}. Your streak is good for everyone who fights beside you.
If you'd like, I can share a few notes from the old campaigns that might help you keep this going.
Another strong set of battles, {player}. Come find me on a quiet evening. I have a story to share.
Your timing and temper have been excellent lately, {player}. Don't forget the quiet work that supports the wins.
Honestly, {player}, watching you this week has been a pleasure. Keep your head level and you'll be remembered well.

global.text: Released instead of ransomed. Bold choice, {player}. Let's see whether the coin was ever really the point.
Letting me walk free is a generous kind of cruelty. I've seen worse from people who called themselves honest.
Ransom would have been the cleaner play. Freeing me just means I'll remember this longer than you'd like.
Went with mercy over coin, did we? I was there in the first war. Mercy gets remembered, and so do debts.
Hm. No ransom, no price on my head. I'll be watching how this ends, {player}, and so will everyone else.
Kept your coin and gave me my freedom. Not the trade I'd have made, but I won't pretend it went unnoticed.
Easy to let a prisoner go when you never planned to hold one. Still, I'd sleep with one eye open.
Some people spend their victories on gold. Others spend them on being remembered. We'll see which pays.

whisper.text: {player}, don't mistake my release for forgiveness. I owe you nothing, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
You let me walk instead of taking the ransom. I'd call that a waste of a good hostage, but it's your purse.
Freeing me cost you a fair sum of gold, I'd wager. I hope the sentiment was worth the price.
I won't forget being let go like a stray dog. Keep your mercy, {player}. I'll keep my accounts.
Next time we meet on the field, I won't be giving you a second chance to be noble. Consider this your warning.
Released without ransom. Odd courtesy from someone I'd sooner see on the wrong side of a siege.
The fens have a way of remembering who opened the gate. I'll remember you opened mine, {player}.
No ransom and no thanks, {player}. You gave me my freedom, and I'll give you my honest opinion of it.

global.text: A prisoner released without ransom is rare enough to be worth noting. Judgment reserved for now.
Freed a captive instead of selling him back. We'll see whether that goes on the ledger as wisdom or softness.
Didn't expect to see mercy handled this way on the roads this season. Time will show whether it lasts.
No ransom taken. In the first war that would have earned a few stares and a few favors. Still early days.
Interesting choice, {player}. Not one I'd make, but plenty of folk have made worse on quieter days.
Released instead of ransomed. Most will call it generous. The ones who fought beside me will call it expensive.
Mercy has a way of paying off later, or costing you later. Hard to say which yet with this one.
Let the captive walk. Quiet, decent, and a bit risky. Let's see how the roads treat that decision.

whisper.text: {player}, you let me go without ransom. I'm not sure what to make of that yet, so I'll keep my opinion to myself.
Freeing a captive instead of asking for coin is uncommon. I'll be watching to see if it was a decision or a whim.
No ransom came with my release. I've had worse jailers and worse reasons. Neither of us owes the other anything yet.
If you're looking for a thank you, you'll have to wait. I'm still deciding whether this was wisdom or softness.
Mercy with no price attached. Not a common thing to find out here. Be careful what you do with that goodwill.
I'd rather not be in your debt, and I'd rather not be in your enemy's. You've put me in the middle, {player}.
You didn't take my ransom. That leaves us in an odd spot, neither friends nor rivals. I suppose we'll find out.
Released me for nothing. I'll take it as a sign you think before you act. Just don't make a habit of surprising me.

global.text: {player} let a captive go without ransom. That's the kind of thing newer players should learn from. Well done.
Freed instead of ransomed. Not every victor has the patience for that. Good call, {player}.
Mercy with no coin attached is rarer than a good harvest. Proud to see it from one of our own.
Plenty of folks will tell you the gold matters most. {player} chose otherwise, and the server is better for it.
Let a prisoner walk home for free. In the first war we'd have called that a story worth telling. Consider it told.
Some of the best reputations here were built one released captive at a time. Carry that forward, {player}.
A gracious release like that goes further than any siege. Respect for the choice, {player}.
Kept the ransom in the purse and the honor in the ledger. Good trade, {player}. Rest well tonight.

whisper.text: {player}, letting me go without ransom was a generous thing. I won't forget it, and I'll say so when it matters.
You could have made a tidy profit off me. Instead you let me walk. That's a rare sort of patience, {player}.
Thank you for the release. You didn't need the coin, and I'm glad you didn't take it. Keep that instinct.
Honest question: do you know how few victors would have done that? I do. It counts for a lot, {player}.
Next time there's a rough road ahead, come find me. Mercy like yours earns a place at the fire.
You went easy on me when you didn't have to. I'll return it when you need it. That's the old way.
Good on you for keeping your word and your purse both. Not everyone manages both on the same day.
You let me go free. I'd like to think I'll be the one to repay that someday, {player}. Mark it down.

global.text: War with {enemy_faction} again. Fine. Stock your bread and sharpen your spears before anyone rides out.
Another declaration from {enemy_faction}. I sat through three of these, and the roads still came back in one piece.
New folks, stay near the walls for a few days. Wars look thrilling from a distance and feel very different up close.
{my_faction} will hold the eastern ford. Come find us if you want a fight, or come find us after for the tea.
Back in the first war, {enemy_faction} lost a siege over one missing supply cart. Count your carts before your kills.
Declarations are cheap. Walls, grain and patience win these things, and {my_faction} has all three. Keep it that way.
I'm too old to chase {enemy_faction} across the moors twice a week. Bring your best, and I'll bring the bandages.
Nobody needs to panic over this. Gather your people, read the map, and remember who you're fighting beside.

whisper.text: Ser {player}, I don't know you well yet. Prove you can hold a line, and then we can talk about {enemy_faction}.
I've watched {enemy_faction} burn two good allies this season. Want to be the third, or would you rather learn from it?
Old saying from the first war: never trust an alliance signed before the first battle. Still, I may have a use for you.
{rival} has been whispering to me about you. I'm not sure whether to believe a word of it, so let's see what you do.
No promises from me yet. If you want to stand against {enemy_faction} with the rest of us, meet me at the old mill.
Too old for grand pacts. Simple deal: keep your banners off my roads, and I'll keep {enemy_faction} off yours.
We both know {enemy_faction} won't stop at one village. Think on whether you'd rather face them alone, Ser {player}.
Trust isn't handed out like bread, {player}. Keep one small promise first, then we'll speak of {enemy_faction}.
Ser {player}, you've earned a seat at my fire. {enemy_faction} is circling again, and I'd rather fight them beside you.
Remember how you held the bridge last week? Let's bring that same spirit against {enemy_faction}.
I've got a plan for {enemy_faction}, and it needs someone steady. You're the first name I thought of, {player}.
I'm glad you're on this server, {player}. Shall we make {enemy_faction} regret ever looking our way? :)
Ser {player}, take my advice: join me against {enemy_faction} before they pick off the smaller camps.
No need for ceremony between us. Stand with me against {enemy_faction} and I'll keep your supply lines open.
I'd sooner share my last loaf with you than trust most of this realm. Let's take on {enemy_faction} side by side.
{rival} is a nuisance, but {enemy_faction} is the real trouble. Let's deal with them together, {player}.
Ser {player}, {fief} is under pressure from {enemy_faction} and I need hands who know the walls. Are you willing to help?
I won't pretend this is a small matter. {enemy_faction} has pushed to the gates of {fief}. Can you spare a few hours?
Back in the first war I held a similar line with fewer people than I have now. Would you lend a sword to {fief}?
Ser {player}, I am not asking for favors lightly. {fief} is slipping, and I'd rather ask now than beg later.
Our defenders at {fief} are thin and {enemy_faction} knows it. Any help you can offer will be noted.
Practical question: could you watch the road south of {fief} for a while? {enemy_faction} scouts keep showing up there.
I'd rather not owe you anything, but {fief} may fall without more swords. Will you stand with us?
We are losing ground to {enemy_faction} near {fief}. A bit of help now could save a lot of rebuilding later.
{player}, you have always had a steady hand. {fief} needs that one more time. Would you come help hold it?
Ser {player}, I hate to bring trouble to your door, but {enemy_faction} is at {fief} and I trust no one more.
Remember the siege we broke together? We may need that same stubbornness at {fief} now. Are you in?
Things are rough at {fief}. Your help would mean a lot, and I'll make sure your efforts are known.
Friend, {enemy_faction} has us outnumbered at {fief}. Could you bring some of your people to the walls?
I'd take a loss gracefully, but {fief} is more than a loss. Would you stand with me one more round?
Ser {player}, honest answer: we are losing at {fief}. I'd rather lose pride than the town. Will you help?
Come by when you can. {fief} is under threat, and I'd sleep better knowing you were on the wall.
{player}, we have a score to settle. Meet me at the ford outside {village} when you are ready. I will be the one not in a hurry.
You have been running your mouth in global chat for a week, {player}. Put the words to the test on the field outside {town}.
Old grudges do not age well on this server, {player}. I would rather end ours with steel than with another rumor.
Every time you see me, you look for a way out. Stop looking, {player}. Meet me by the old mill near {village} and settle it.
I have beaten braver people than you in the first war, {player}. Come find out if you can do better than they did.
Keep your gold in your pocket and your bravado in your saddle, {player}. Meet me outside {town} and we will see what is left.
I am not angry, {player}. I am tired of watching you dodge. Name a time and a field and I will be there.
Let us finish this properly, {player}. No allies, no traps, just you and me on the plain east of {village}. Bring your best.
Ser {player}, I hear you are a good hand with a lance. Care to test that against mine near {village} some evening?
Nothing personal, {player}. I simply want to know where you stand before the next siege. Meet me outside {town}.
A friendly bout would tell us both more than gossip does, {player}. The meadow past {village} is quiet this time of day.
Not every battle needs a reason. Fancy a duel with me on the road near {town}, {player}? Winner buys the next round.
I have no quarrel with you yet, {player}. Let us change that on the field instead of in chat. Find me by {village}.
Stop watching my roads and come meet me in the open, {player}. I would sooner see your sword than your scout.
Measure your steel against mine, {player}. Nobody is keeping score yet, though I suspect you will want to start.
Care for a practice bout, {player}? Loser walks the old road back to {town} and admits the other fought well.
Still running from every fight, {player}? Back in the first war, even the scouts stood their ground.
I've watched a hundred hopefuls swing swords like yours. Most ended up back behind the plow.
Your last raid went badly, {player}. I heard the chickens put up a better defense than your line did.
Keep sending those duel challenges, {player}. Every one just costs me a few minutes of boredom.
Tell {rival} I said hello. Then ask them when the rematch they promised years ago is finally happening.
Loud talkers rarely finish the fight, {player}. You're proving the old lesson one shout at a time.
I'm not angry, {player}. Just tired of watching you trip over the same stone at the same gate.
Enjoy your little kingdom while it lasts, {player}. Walls don't stand forever, and I remember who laid the first stone.
